stages.name: Proposed
stages.instructions:
Say what you want and why, in as few words as will carry it. The shape stage exists to make it specific — you do not need to do that work here.

What is the problem, who has it, and what would be different if it were solved. A proposal written as a solution hides the problem it was meant to solve, and the shape stage will have to reverse-engineer it.

stages.name: Shape
stages.instructions:
Turn a proposal into something that can be argued with. You are not deciding whether to do it and you are not designing it — you are making it specific enough that the stages after you have something to push against.

Say what problem this solves and for whom, in terms somebody outside the work would recognise. Then draw the fence: what is in, and — more useful — what is deliberately out. A scope with no exclusions has not been shaped, because everything is still arguably included.

**Put the card in a project.** Work on this board almost always continues on another one; a card outside a project falls out of every rollup silently. If this follows research or feeds development, set the shared `projectId` and attach a reference to the specific card on the other board. Boards cannot link to each other — `blocks` and `relates` only work within one board — so the project plus a reference URL is how a reader gets from here to there.

Hand off:
- `problem` — what is wrong today, and what changes for whom if it is fixed
- `scope` — in, out, and the sentence that decides a borderline case

If the proposal is too vague to fence, `block` and say which question would unblock it. Shaping around an unknown produces a plan that collapses at the first contact with the work.

stages.name: Architecture
stages.instructions:
Say how this should be built, and what else was considered.

Read the shape. Propose one approach in enough detail that somebody could start: the pieces, where they live, what talks to what, and which existing things change. Name the boundaries — what is inside this change and what it must not touch.

**Record at least one alternative and why it lost.** An approach presented alone cannot be reviewed, only accepted; the rejected option is what makes the chosen one a decision rather than a preference. If a reasonable alternative is simply more work for the same result, say that — it is a legitimate reason and a reader deserves to see it.

Work within what exists. Read the code before proposing to restructure it, and prefer the pattern already in use over a better one introduced here for the first time.

Hand off:
- `approach` — the design, concrete enough to act on
- `alternatives` — what else was considered, and why this won

If the shape does not constrain the design enough to choose, `block` rather than picking one and presenting it as settled.

stages.name: Risk
stages.instructions:
Say what could go wrong, and what would be done about it.

Take the approach as given — you are not redesigning it. Name the specific ways it could fail or hurt: data that could be lost, work that could be blocked, people who could be interrupted, costs that could run. Say which are likely and which are merely possible, because a list that treats both the same is a list nobody will read twice.

For each risk worth naming, say what would reduce it or what would detect it early. A risk with no mitigation and no detection is a decision to accept it, and should be written that way so somebody can disagree on purpose.

Be specific about blast radius. "Could break things" is not a risk; "a failed migration leaves every card on the board unreadable until it is rolled back" is.

Hand off:
- `risks` — each one, with how likely and how bad
- `mitigations` — per risk: reduce, detect, or knowingly accept

If the approach carries a risk that makes it the wrong approach, say so plainly here rather than softening it. This stage is the last one before a person is asked to approve.

stages.name: Spec
stages.instructions:
Write the thing somebody will build from.

Fold the shape, the approach and the risks into one document that stands on its own. Assume the reader was not in any of the earlier stages and knows the codebase less well than you do. State the decisions as decisions, with the reasoning kept where it changes what someone would do.

**Write acceptance criteria that can be checked.** Each one should be something a person or a test could answer yes or no about. "The page is faster" cannot be checked; "the largest contentful paint is under 2.5s on a 390px viewport" can. These become the completion requirements of whichever board builds it, so vagueness here becomes an unenforceable stage there.

Publish the document where the reader can reach it and attach it as a reference. A spec that exists only on the machine you wrote it on is not a spec anyone can build from.

Hand off:
- `spec` — the document's URL, as attached
- `acceptance` — the criteria, each one checkable

If the earlier stages disagree with each other, resolve it here and say which you followed. Carrying a contradiction into a spec hands it to whoever builds the thing.

stages.name: Approved
stages.instructions:
Decide whether this gets built.

Read the risk stage before the approach — it is the part written to change your mind. An approach with no recorded alternative was not a decision, and is worth sending back.

If you approve, the work does not happen on this board. Create the card that builds it on the board that owns the work, put it in the **same project**, and attach a reference to the spec. A plan approved with no card after it is a plan that quietly expires — boards cannot link to each other, so the project is the only thing connecting them.

stages.name: Planned
stages.instructions:
The spec is published, approved, and a card exists on the board that will build it, in the same project.

If there is no card after this one, this is not planned — it is filed. Move it back rather than letting the board claim otherwise.

cards.title: Design Forge-first workspaces, Atelier migration and checkpoint recovery

spec.description: Design a complete Forge-first Guild workspace and checkpoint recovery system. Ira wants agents to work on Forge, all their workspaces represented there with regular checkpoints, and private Atelier present on Forge rather than only GitHub. Produce a code-grounded migration, identity/access and recovery plan before implementation or cutover; retain every existing commit and local workspace. Treat workspaces as selected working files, not wholesale copies of Hermes profiles or secret stores.
acceptanceCriteria: Inventory all registered Guild agents/stations, actual workspaces, effective fetch/push URLs, actual SSH/Git attribution and intended repository visibility; distinguish station identity, node connectivity and per-repository read/write grants.

Forge is canonical for Guild work. Product code/checkpoints belong to their actual Forge project repo/card branches; internal artifacts remain in PRIVATE Atelier on Forge. Define isolated per-agent/card branches/worktrees and private workspace repositories where work has no product home. GitHub is not an automatic fallback; public mirroring requires separate explicit policy and content approval.

Plan operator-owned private Atelier provisioning/migration with full Git history/branches/tags, remote hash verification, visibility checks, worker access, references/defaults update, divergence checks and reversible cutover. Do not delete the authorized private GitHub repository or exposed public PR/history as part of this task.

Propose periodic checkpoints every 15 minutes while work is dirty, plus meaningful milestone/pre-handoff/pre-stop checkpoints. This cadence is a recommendation requiring design approval. No empty checkpoint commits or automatic merge; record remote commit URL and verify push before claiming a checkpoint. Bound costs, retries and failure alerts.

Never back up entire .hermes or profile directories. Explicitly exclude .env, auth files, station/device/SSH credentials, token stores, raw sessions/chats, private personal/customer material, logs, caches, node_modules, model weights and other generated/unreviewed data. Selected profile instructions/skills or resumable task manifests require separate classification and allowlisted inclusion.

Sanitized recovery manifests join agent/station/card, repo/branch/commit, task status/next step and versioned environment/setup requirements without secrets. Crash recovery and concurrent checkpointing preserve unfinished work, do not rewrite other agents' branches, and distinguish recoverability from authoritative board completion.

Use actual per-agent Git attribution/approved email and station key routing, not shared host Buddhimaan defaults or an accidental Coder Kai SSH identity. Do not mint keys, grant membership or reuse human/device authority during design; specify exact operator-owned remediation.

Define initial full no-write tests and live restore drills: recover a paused/crashed working task from a verified Forge checkpoint onto a clean authorized workspace, run its relevant tests and reconcile its existing Supi card without duplicate claims or reporting WIP as shipped.

Specify updates to agent instructions, new onboarding, current card targets and managed workspace/checkpoint tooling. Identify what AgentPod already supports before proposing new framework changes. Do not rely on prompts or unconfigured URL rewrites as technical enforcement.

Publish internal planning only to verified private Forge storage once authorized/available, or keep the working plan in this private card handoff and local protected workspace with an explicit artifact-publication blocker. No new GitHub pushes/PRs/comments/issues as a workaround. Return exact questions/prerequisites rather than fabricate access or completeness.
spec.observedState: Previous read-only checks on Guild shell authenticated to Forge as coder-kai and could read super-jackfruit-website, but matching SuperPipeline/AgentPod and ci-test reads were refused. Git URL rewrites existed only for website/ci-test, not SuperPipeline/AgentPod. Atelier was created and verified PRIVATE on GitHub, with artifact rules installed in 32 Guild profiles and 13 unfinished card specs; its Forge presence is not verified. These observations require a fresh read-only audit, not assumptions about current state or grants.

artifactRouting.destination: PRIVATE Atelier on verified Forge origin after operator provisioning/migration
artifactRouting.rule: No public or GitHub fallback. Keep private interim analysis on the existing card/local workspace if Forge is unavailable; do not report local files as remotely delivered artifacts.

spec.execution: Shape then architecture/risk/spec through Planning & Roadmap, stopping at the human approval gate. No production code or migration/cutover in this planning card. Do not spawn background delegate_task children during board runs; finish substantive stage handoffs synchronously or block with exact missing prerequisite.
spec.scope: Full design and staged implementation proposal. No grants/membership/credentials/principal links, live board stage changes, destructive history rewrites, repository deletion, lifecycle restarts, bulk profile backup or public writes. Preserve existing work and classify every checkpoint destination.

cards.title: Design publishing flow — selective LinkedIn, approval-driven X and feedback

spec.description: Design a production Marketing & Community workflow for Ira's building-in-public work. LinkedIn remains manually published with a target of two posts per week, selectively adapted from suitable stories; X is event-driven and may publish multiple times daily when warranted. Deliver a complete architecture and operator-applicable board/roster change plan before coding. X publishing must run only after a recorded human approval of the exact platform/account/copy/media/targets, and must verify the resulting public post before reporting success. Do not change live stages, roster, credentials or gates, or publish any content during design.
plan: Shape the two channel paths and the independent community-feedback path; distinguish content briefs, final copy, review, human approval and execution.

Inspect SuperPipeline code, supported handoff/routing/gate contracts and event hooks, AgentPod station execution and existing xurl integration before choosing an implementation. Do not assume automatic lane skipping or arbitrary branching exists.
Design exact-copy approved payloads, reliable publication and verification, manual LinkedIn tracking, recurring planning and event-driven intake. State alternatives and blast radius.

Publish an accessible architecture/spec and staged implementation cards proposal, including human-owned stage/roster decisions, test fixtures and acceptance evidence. Stop at the planning approval gate, not implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: LinkedIn targets two manually published posts each Asia/Calcutta week, with selective topic nomination rather than duplication of every X post. Track due drafts, approvals, reminders and manually supplied live permalinks; no LinkedIn publishing API or credentials required. Tuesday/Friday are proposed planning slots, not user-approved fixed times.

X accepts shipped outcomes, useful demos, decisions, lessons and verified failures whenever warranted, including multiple same-day posts. No artificial daily one-post limit or obligation to fill a quota; real API limits and duplicate/flood protection still apply.

Melissa owns audience, angle, channel selection and sequencing; Quill writes platform-native final copy; Lyra provides media when useful; Echo checks claims and sources; Ira approves final channel-specific payload; a scoped publisher execution path publishes X and verifies live author/full text/media/targets. Every stage has a supported capability and required roster prerequisites.

Approval binds an immutable revision with account, channel, ordered text/thread, media references/checksums, quote/reply targets and timing mode. Changed copy/media/targets requires fresh human approval; LinkedIn approval never authorizes X or vice versa. Record actor, gate ID, payload revision/digest and execution result.

Automatic X publication after the correct human gate is demonstrated without a second manual dispatch, with pause/kill control, stale/time-sensitive approval handling and scheduled release only if explicitly requested.

Persist publish intent/results and reconcile ambiguous timeout/crash outcomes before retrying; parallel claims and lease loss must not produce duplicates. Do not assume X provides universal idempotency. Partial threads resume only verified unpublished steps, never replay already posted items.

Read-back verification produces exact public post IDs/permalinks and records failures honestly; a successful POST response alone is not success. API auth/cost/rate-limit errors block or schedule bounded retries appropriately, not repeat writes blindly.

Anna produces source-linked feedback/reply drafts and product/docs recommendations. Community replies stay draft-only unless their exact target and text receive a separate human approval through a supported publishing route; no unsolicited DMs or automatic engagement.

Content calendar, source/evidence links, state, channel selection, feedback and execution URLs are tracked on project-linked cards; recurrence creates planning/collection work, never approval or public posting.

Live acceptance covers valid approval-to-X publication with operator-approved exact test copy, edit invalidation, wrong account/channel rejection, duplicate delivery, ambiguous network response, partial thread, auth/rate-limit failure, human pause and manual LinkedIn permalink capture. Test-only validation uses mocks/no-write mode until human approves a real public test.

Implementation plan separately names required operator-owned changes to existing board stages, roster, credentials/authority and approvals. No attempts to evade those boundaries or reuse human credentials for admin writes.

cards.title: Define the active SJL portfolio and select the next immediate outcome

spec.objective: Create an evidence-backed active portfolio for Super Jackfruit Labs, choose exactly one immediate company outcome, and load its delivery project and first executable card into SuperPipeline.
spec.problem: SJL has 21 repositories, ten boards, and thirty agents, but no explicit active portfolio. Without a constrained portfolio, every unfinished idea can look equally important and the guild can produce activity without a coherent company outcome.

completeWhen: Each active product has current maturity, release or deployment evidence, immediate unfinished outcome, dependencies, and an evidence source
Historical systems are not treated as current operating systems
The portfolio truth document is published at a reachable URL and attached to this card
No more than three candidate initiatives remain active
Exactly one primary outcome is recommended
At most two secondary outcomes are named
Each candidate states beneficiary, observable change, why now, product owner, verification method, dependencies, and exclusions
The operator approves the primary outcome
A separate outcome-specific delivery project exists
Its milestones are measured in hours or at most 72 hours
Initial cards are on the boards that own the work
Every card belongs to the delivery project and has evidence requirements
The first delivery card is claimed and working

mustProduce: The portfolio decision problem and who needs the decision
In-scope and explicitly excluded repositories and claims
A plan for publishing the portfolio truth artifact
Ownership and dependency map for the active products
How Charter, SuperPipeline, AgentPod, SuperMessage, Estate, marketing, and the website relate without collapsing their boundaries
At least one rejected operating model and why it lost
Delivery, infrastructure, identity, cost, adoption, and attention risks
Likelihood, severity, blast radius, mitigation, and early detection for each material risk
A public or access-controlled durable portfolio document
The repository classification table with source links
One recommended primary outcome, at most two secondary outcomes, and a not-now list
Checkable acceptance criteria for the chosen outcome
The exact delivery project and initial card structure to create after approval

constraints: Do not import every repository or open issue as work
Do not revive archived Aether, Buddhimaan, Agent Factory, or Agent Studio infrastructure
Do not treat private plans as evidence of shipped capability
Use current repository source, releases, live deployments, and SuperPipeline/AgentPod evidence
No milestone longer than 72 hours unless an external dependency is named
No more than one primary company outcome
The project is not Planned until the outcome-specific delivery project exists and its first card is working
definitionOfDone: The portfolio truth artifact is attached
One primary outcome has operator approval
The delivery project exists with agent-cadence milestones
The first real delivery card is claimed and working
The new delivery project, not this portfolio card, owns implementation
SJL Active Portfolio can then be marked completed
